before=IM epinephrine into the anterolateral thigh, repeated, plus aggressive fluids comes FIRST. An infusion is for the patient who has had repeat IM doses and is still shocked.
before=In a trauma patient this is a diagnosis of exclusion. Find and treat the bleeding first; warm, well-perfused extremities with a slow heart rate are the clue, not the proof.

before=Pads on and the pacer set up in parallel. These drips are the bridge to pacing, not a substitute for it.
before=Resuscitate before you induce. A pressor drawn up, or better, a drip already running BEFORE the drugs go in — induction plus positive pressure is when these patients arrest.
before=The pressor buys time to the cath lab or the lytic. Nothing on this card opens an artery.

detail=The rate on this row is the ADULT fixed rate and is withheld here. The pediatric Surviving Sepsis Campaign guideline suggests AGAINST vasopressin as a routine addition in pediatric septic shock, and publishes no weight-based dose to give in its place — so this card will not compute one. If it is used, it is an individualized decision made with critical care / pediatric intensive care, not a number read off an aid.
